subject.title: Config: scaffold compaction loop guard settings

question: Should OpenClaw accept a reserved `agents.defaults.compaction.guard` config namespace for future saturated-session compaction behavior, or keep loop-guard controls under the current `tools.loopDetection.postCompactionGuard` and canonical issue design?
rationale: The branch is focused, but new config/default surfaces are compatibility-sensitive and current main already has an adjacent post-compaction loop guard under a different namespace; accepting this PR would publish API direction before maintainer agreement.

options.title: Defer To Canonical Issue
options.body: Keep this PR open but paused while maintainers decide the config/API shape in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/48238 and the existing post-compaction guard path.

options.title: Adopt This Namespace
options.body: Accept this PR's reserved config surface after adding upgrade-proofed docs/tests and explaining how it will coexist with or supersede `tools.loopDetection.postCompactionGuard`.

options.title: Close And Redesign
options.body: Close this branch if maintainers decide the separate `agents.defaults.compaction.guard` namespace should not become public config.

recommendation.title: Defer To Canonical Issue
recommendation.body: Keep this PR open but paused while maintainers decide the config/API shape in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/48238 and the existing post-compaction guard path.

likelyOwner.reason: The canonical issue review identifies steipete as the strongest recent routing candidate for compaction safeguard schema and post-compaction guard policy decisions.
